purpose: Skeleton-first shoulder-girdle geometry audit. Test the a003 mesh-driven clavicle/scapula spans against independent osseous morphometry.
findings: The a003 clavicle SC-to-AC straight span (~223 mm) is anatomically implausible. It exceeds a male CT true curved clavicle mean (~150 mm) by ~73 mm and even exceeds a male cadaver 3D centreline mean (~167 mm) by ~56 mm. A straight endpoint chord cannot legitimately be longer than the true curved bone length.

The a003 scapular GH-to-inferior-angle span (~212 mm) is strongly suspicious, but it must not be compared as if it were the same measurement as whole scapular height. In the male source, mean whole height/width are ~148/108 mm (bounding diagonal ~183.4 mm; even height+1SD and width+1SD give ~195.3 mm). The a003 GH-to-inferior span exceeds those scale checks, so scapular geometry remains a RED rebuild candidate, but the exact amount of shortening is not frozen.

The clavicle defect is directly confirmed by measurement semantics; the scapular scale check strongly supports the same broad-shoulder mesh-driven problem but requires landmark-compatible 3D retargeting before an exact correction is claimed.

The previously corroborated GH depth relative to the acromion does not rescue the overall shoulder-girdle proportions. Local joint-depth placement can be reasonable while the global SC-AC and scapular spans are wrong.
The final skeleton-first shoulder must therefore retarget SC, AC, scapular body, acromion and glenoid geometry independently of the r95 shoulder width, then the mesh must be narrowed/refit around it.
canonical_requirements: Define scapular superior angle, inferior angle, medial border/spine root, acromion, coracoid and glenoid centre from an evidence-backed local scapular frame before selecting any GH-to-inferior target.
Represent clavicle with a curved centreline or equivalent non-bone reference geometry; SC and AC remain true endpoints.
Use male clavicle endpoint/centreline corridors and preserve the fact that endpoint distance must be shorter than curved true length.
Keep AC and GH centres distinct and anatomically separated.
After girdle retargeting, recompute shoulder breadth from skeleton plus realistic deltoid/soft-tissue thickness rather than preserving the old mesh breadth.
acceptance_tests: SC-to-AC endpoint distance is less than the corresponding clavicle curved centreline length.
Clavicle centreline and endpoint measures fall inside a multi-source adult male corridor or have a documented stature-specific justification.
Scapular GH-to-inferior-angle distance must be checked against a landmark-compatible 3D scapular envelope (height + width + glenoid position), not against height alone.
Glenoid size/orientation and glenoid-to-acromion relationship remain within source corridors.
Bilateral mirror symmetry is preserved in the canonical skeleton.
Shoulder-complex movement tests are rerun because changing SC/AC/scapular geometry changes GH path and lever arms.

audit_correction_2026_10_08.reason: Earlier wording treated GH-to-inferior-angle distance as if it must be less than superior-to-inferior scapular height. That is not a valid hard invariant because GH is laterally offset; the Euclidean span can exceed vertical height.
audit_correction_2026_10_08.correction: Use a 3D height/width/glenoid-position envelope. Clavicle chord-vs-centreline invariant remains valid.
audit_correction_2026_10_08.result: Scapula remains strongly suspicious but exact shortening is not claimed from a height-only comparison.
